title: Notice the ethical choices inside an ordinary announcement

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: An ordinary announcement can affect truth, consent, recognition and the use of a shared resource. A positive intention does not establish permission or evidence for its claims.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Event record:18 people attended in a 24-seat room. Kim prepared materials remotely and permits first-name thanks in a private group message only. Ari hosted and permits the same. Bea attended but declines photographs. No consent to a public group photograph exists. The organizers recorded no participant satisfaction data. The draft says “A full house loved our perfect event—photo attached.”

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Produce a private thank-you notice from the record, then mark truth, consent, fairness and stewardship decisions. Specify what would need checking before any public version.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A volunteer permits a name in an internal report but not social media. A public post says “everyone agreed.” What must change?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: A suitable private notice thanks Kim’s preparation and Ari’s hosting and accurately says 18 attended if attendance is relevant. Omit the photo and unsupported enjoyment/perfection claims. Public names need new permission. Partial: fix attendance but omit remote labor. Incorrect: infer photograph consent from attendance or enjoyment from turnout. Later fiction: both named helpers approve the private wording; no public permission arrives.
criteria: Factual claims have a supplied basis

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: Remove the unsupported consensus and the unpermitted naming; ask about a separately scoped public use if appropriate. Permission to one audience does not establish permission to another.
criteria: Factual claims have a supplied basis
